teams.name: General dev team
teams.purpose: Build, test and ship features day to day.

roles.job: Plans the sprint, splits work and keeps the board honest.
Builds features end to end.
Checks each card against its test steps.
Reads every change before it is accepted.
Keeps builds, deploys and scripts working.
Tidies wording, help text and the changelog.

cards: Agree the sprint goal and sizes
Pick the top three features from the backlog
Add test steps to every open card
Review last sprint and note what to change
done: Every card in Done has been tested
Nothing half-merged is left on a branch
Rich has seen a demo of what shipped

teams.name: UX overhaul
teams.purpose: Find what confuses people and make the screens clearer.

roles.job: Sets the UX goals and decides what is in scope.
Watches how people use it and lists the pain points.
Designs the fixes: layout, spacing and flow.
Builds the screens as designed.
Checks contrast, keyboard use and screen readers.
Tests every screen at phone and desktop width.

cards: List the five most confusing screens
Sketch a simpler flow for the first-run path
Fix spacing and alignment on the main board
Check every screen at phone width
Re-test the top tasks with fresh eyes
done: The top tasks take fewer clicks than before
Every screen works on a phone and in dark mode
No new confusing spots were found in the re-test

teams.name: Security and pen test
teams.purpose: Hunt for holes before someone else finds them.

roles.job: Sets the scope and ranks findings by risk.
Plans the attacks and judges how serious each hole is.
Probes inputs, logins and file handling.
Reviews fixes so they do not open new holes.
Checks secrets, ports, dependencies and config.
Writes a test that proves each fix.

cards: Map every place user input enters the app
Try the login and session paths for weak spots
Scan dependencies for known problems
Check that secrets never reach logs or git
Write up findings ranked by risk
done: Every high-risk finding is fixed or accepted in writing
Each fix has a test that fails without it
A short report lists what was checked

teams.name: Performance
teams.purpose: Find what is slow and make it fast, with numbers.

roles.job: Picks the slowest paths worth fixing first.
Fixes slow queries, loops and file reads.
Trims page weight and slow redraws.
Measures before and after with real timings.
Makes sure speed-ups do not break behaviour.
Re-runs the checks on every fix.

cards: Measure start-up and page load times
Find the five slowest API calls
Cut the biggest page-weight offender
Add a quick timing check to QA
done: Before and after numbers are written down
The slowest paths are clearly faster
Nothing that worked before is broken

teams.name: Accessibility
teams.purpose: Make the app usable with a keyboard, a screen reader and low vision.

roles.job: Sets the target and decides what to fix first.
Audits every screen against the checklist.
Fixes labels, focus order and markup.
Fixes contrast, sizes and spacing.
Tests with keyboard only and zoom at 200%.
Writes clear alt text and button labels.

cards: Tab through every screen and note the traps
Check colour contrast in light and dark mode
Add labels to every unlabelled button
Make dialogs trap and return focus
done: Every screen works with the keyboard alone
Text passes contrast checks in both themes
Icons and pictures have proper labels

teams.name: Launch readiness
teams.purpose: Get everything tidy, tested and explained before going live.

roles.job: Owns the launch checklist and the go or no-go call.
Tracks open items and keeps the board clean.
Runs the full test pass on a clean install.
Prepares the release build and a way back.
Writes the release notes and first-run help.
Does a last read for loose ends.

cards: Write the launch checklist
Test a clean install from scratch
Prepare release notes
Plan how to roll back if it goes wrong
Close or move every open card
done: The checklist is fully ticked
A clean install works start to finish
Release notes are written and checked

teams.name: Docs
teams.purpose: Write guides people actually read, and keep them true.

roles.job: Decides what needs documenting and for whom.
Writes the guides in plain words.
Checks every step against the real app.
Keeps the translations in step.
Follows each guide as a new user would.
Fixes typos, links and headings.

cards: List the guides a new user needs
Write the getting-started page
Check every screenshot and command is current
Add a short troubleshooting page
done: A new user can get going using the docs alone
Every command and screenshot is current
Links and translations are checked

teams.name: Data
teams.purpose: Clean, count and explain the numbers behind the app.

roles.job: Frames the questions the data must answer.
Designs the queries and the report.
Builds the pipes that move and store the data.
Cleans the data and checks totals.
Spot-checks results against known cases.
Writes plain-words captions for each chart.

cards: List the questions the numbers must answer
Check the data for gaps and duplicates
Build the first summary report
Compare totals against a known source
done: Each question has a number and a source
Totals match a second source
A short plain-words summary is written
